overlap_rationale:
Two recurring skills, not two color-specific policies: acquire_block and deliver_block. Each has a red occurrence and a blue occurrence in every trajectory. All 8,897 source actions are retained, including initial approach, closing, lifting, release, retreat, settling and terminal holds. Segments are half-open in actions and include observations at both endpoints. All proposed endpoints have been inspected. No same-skill segments overlap; adjacent different-skill occurrences deliberately share long transitions. In trajectory order demo10300 through demo10311, the three shared intervals (red acquisition->delivery; red delivery->blue acquisition; blue acquisition->delivery) are respectively: 00 [75,182),[265,415),[445,562); 01 [76,184),[267,418),[447,564); 02 [78,188),[273,427),[454,576); 03 [74,185),[268,420),[450,566); 04 [73,180),[263,414),[443,558); 05 [79,190),[274,428),[457,578); 06 [77,187),[271,424),[453,571); 07 [72,178),[259,408),[439,552); 08 [74,181),[264,416),[445,561); 09 [75,183),[266,419),[448,564); 10 [71,177),[258,407),[438,551); 11 [76,184),[267,420),[449,566). Acquisition->delivery overlaps are 106-122 actions (5.30-6.10 s); delivery->acquisition overlaps are 149-154 actions (7.45-7.70 s), not short boundary tails. Boundaries were retained based on individually inspected states, not equal-duration partitions: delivery entries span open-finger descent at TCP world z 0.088-0.160 m for red and 0.108-0.178 m for blue; acquisition exits span closed-finger elevated early translation, red center z 0.280-0.283 m and blue 0.287-0.293 m. Blue acquisition starts while red is still held and descending over its region (red z 0.084-0.169 m), before opening or settling; red delivery ends only after red is released, TCP has retreated and traversed toward blue, fingers are open and TCP is above blue at z about 0.267 m. Thus both neighbors can finish the actual transition rather than require a single cut pose. No data establish recovery from lateral grasp misses, dropped objects, unexpected wall contact, disturbed blocks or arbitrary arm configurations; greater temporal overlap is not greater spatial/contact-error coverage.
Shared implementation contract for all six separate Diffusion Policy candidates: use the supplied 20 Hz pd_joint_pos action contract, seven absolute Panda joint targets (rad) and one dimensionless gripper command, clipped to supplied limits. qpos[0:7]/qvel[0:7] are arm rad/rad/s; qpos[7:9]/qvel[7:9] are finger m/m/s. Gripper +1 requests 0.04 m per finger, -1 requests -0.01 m; actual grasped finger readings near 0.0183 m are not commanded target widths. All candidates use the SAME observation/action normalizer fitted once on the complete original demonstrations, never per skill, role or overlap. Geometric transformations are computed in physical units before shared scaling; no per-skill rescaling. Drop the two constant zero drawer compatibility channels from learnable conditioning. State inputs are available causally; front images were inspected for grounding but vision-only deployment is not established. World poses are metre/wxyz; use sign-invariant rotations or rotation matrices. Past finite differences use dt=0.05 s; object velocities are derived, not measured qvel channels. Starting research configuration: H=16 future action steps and causal observation history, receding-horizon execution; horizons and any numeric tolerances other than the task contract are tunable hypotheses, not measured robustness. Train only on valid within-segment action/future-observation windows, mask terminal padding and avoid stitching red and blue segments as if contiguous. Split by original trajectory, with both skills and all copies of each overlap in the same split; balance roles and phases to avoid holds and shared samples dominating. Retain unique source indices for weighting and evaluation.
Interface includes an intended object/goal role token, mapped to red_pose/red_goal or blue_pose/blue_goal, and the other object's state. For acquire_block this denotes the object to acquire NEXT; the other object may still need incoming placement/release. For deliver_block it denotes the object being packed, even if not yet grasped; an optional pending-object role enables its exit approach. Role metadata are segment-purpose labels for training, not timestep inputs. A caller/learned task selector must supply or infer these roles from causal scene and invocation intent; this is an explicitly declared interface, not an assumed deployment facility. All data are red-first and then blue; arbitrary order/goal assignment is untested. Do not immediately switch intended object just because the contract predicate becomes true while still holding it. Preserve observation history and previous issued commands across policy transfer, or train masked-history resets from all overlap phases. A role token must be latched through its manipulation, and the outgoing policy's learned retreat/approach must not silently change payload identity.
Completion is precisely the supplied contract: all rotated object corners projected to world xy must lie in the assigned square of half-width 0.06 m, with center |z-0.036|<=0.011 m, for BOTH objects in one observation. Cubes have half-size 0.02 m. Neither opening, low velocity, sustained holding nor TCP clearance is required by that predicate. The demonstrations nevertheless open, allow center z to settle from about 0.0455 to 0.036 m, retreat to TCP z about 0.3165 m and hold. Keep these useful interface actions, but do not invent extra task-success requirements. Candidate readiness heads distinguish task containment from safe manipulation transfer. Fixture boxes from the supplied contract have rim tops at 0.09 m. Representative front images at demo10300 0/120/280, demo10307 310/505 and demo10305 752 support the open-tray, top-grasp, release/retreat interpretation; numeric decisions use synchronized states, not pixel-derived precision.
